A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NeuroKalman work, and all supplied text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. V1 includes Appendix A; v2 ends after the references. These are identifiable content differences rather than extraction gaps.

before.justification: V1 reports original TravelUAV/AirSim navigation results, component ablations, and trajectory analyses in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains original navigation experiments and adds low-data training, post-hoc Kalman filtering, and memory-threshold results in Section 4.

M1.justification: The GRU prior, attention-based memory retrieval, confidence-gated storage, learned Kalman fusion, waypoint prediction, and auxiliary losses remain unchanged. The default memory insertion threshold remains 0.5; the added threshold experiments test variants of the existing method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate continuous aerial navigation using TravelUAV's UAV-Need-Help dataset, retaining seen, unseen-map, unseen-object, Easy/Hard, and assistance-level coverage. V2's added experiments reuse L1 Test-Seen; the removed trajectory examples do not represent separate task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds TravelUAV + Post-KF, applying constant-velocity Kalman filtering to predicted waypoints (Table 6). It removes the MBGRU comparator from v1's structural-decoupling experiment (Appendix Table 5). Comparator membership in the main benchmark Tables 1–2 is unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds a distinct training condition using only 10% of trajectories without full-data pretraining, with uniform trajectory sampling and Easy/Hard distribution checks. It also introduces post-hoc filtering and memory-threshold evaluation settings. The original full-data initialization followed by 10% fine-tuning, benchmark splits, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds controls testing dependence on full-data pretraining, whether output-space smoothing explains the gains, and sensitivity to memory insertion thresholds. It removes v1's structural-decoupling and auxiliary-loss ablations and the top-down/front-view failure analyses. The gain, memory-length, and aggregate drift analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V2 Table 3 newly reports NeuroKalman means and standard deviations over three randomly sampled 10% trajectory subsets and states that sampling uses fixed seeds. This uncertainty reporting concerns the new experiment; no increased repetition count is reported for retained results.

E6.justification: The new no-full-pretraining experiment reports NeuroKalman NE 85.89 ± 2.71 and SR 22.70 ± 0.87, versus TravelUAV's 122.63 and 13.19 (v2 Table 3). Post-KF and threshold results are also added. MBGRU, auxiliary-loss ablation results, and two qualitative examples disappear. Tables 1–2, matched gain/memory-length tables, and Figures 3–4 retain their results.

T1.justification: V2 removes Appendix A.1's error-dynamics assumptions, claimed bounded-error contraction argument, and covariance-weighted anchor-regularization formulation (v1 Equations 10–14). These are substantive theoretical removals without replacement. The main Bayesian, retrieval, and fusion equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: recursive Bayesian navigation, prediction–correction decoupling, the attention/KDE relationship, drift mitigation, and data-efficient fine-tuning with improved generalization.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly interprets the retained 10% experiment as limited fine-tuning and adds explanations involving MLLM capacity, semantic correction versus geometric smoothing, and noisy memory anchors. It removes the appendix's sample-complexity, module-collapse, and landmark-failure explanations. The stated limitation concerning GRU information decay remains unchanged.

D1.justification: V2's abstract adds a project repository address with a promise of future code release. Existing hardware, backbone models, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, and auxiliary-loss coefficient remain unchanged. The PDF does not establish that the promised code is already available.

R1.justification: Four references supporting the removed appendix disappear: Bishop and Nasrabadi (2006), Miller and Hardt (2018), Savinov et al. (2018), and Guu et al. (2020). Section 2 and the main positioning against prior navigation, memory, and filtering research remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most retained prose and the main section hierarchy are unchanged. V2 locally revises the data-efficiency discussion, adds experimental discussion and acknowledgements, removes the appendix structure, and updates affiliations, author-role markers, and publication text.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 3, 6, and 7 while removing v1's appendix Tables 5–6 and both multi-panel trajectory Figures 5–6. The retained fusion and memory-length tables are moved and renumbered, Figure 4 is relocated, and Figure 2's illustrative input labels are revised. The supporting visual material is substantially reorganized.

improvement.justification: The new experiment without full-data pretraining and its subset variability estimates strengthen the central data-efficiency evidence; post-KF and threshold controls add useful checks. These benefits are partly offset by losing direct structural and auxiliary-loss ablations and trajectory cases. The removed contraction argument was itself incomplete: v1's Equation 13 did not establish that the combined error-propagation factor was contractive. Overall, the empirical support improves, but the gains are limited by lost diagnostic evidence.
